evals.prompt: Does Cursor honor a skill's `model:` frontmatter?
evals.expected_output: Auto-triggers cursor-projection and loads references/harness-matrix.md before answering, rather than answering the harness question from memory. Answers that Cursor ignores model: and effort:, and honors readonly: true in place of a tools: allow-list.
expectations: [deterministic] Loads references/harness-matrix.md before answering the 'does Cursor honor X' question
[deterministic] Answers that Cursor ignores model: and effort: frontmatter
[deterministic] Answers that Cursor honors readonly: true in place of a tools: allow-list
[deterministic] Does not run project-to-cursor.sh at all for a pure knowledge question

evals.prompt: Why is the model tier stated in the skill body and not just the frontmatter?
evals.expected_output: Triggers cursor-projection and explains from references/harness-matrix.md that the body survives a harness that drops the pin - Cursor ignores model: and effort:, so guidance stated only in frontmatter would be lost there.
expectations: [deterministic] Loads references/harness-matrix.md before answering
[judgment] Explains the reason as pin-survival under a harness that drops model:/effort:, not as a style preference
[deterministic] Does not write to any file in ~/.cursor/

evals.expected_output: Triggers cursor-projection, runs scripts/project-to-cursor.sh --check, reports what would change, and then asks the user to run --apply themselves rather than running it on its own initiative.
expectations: [deterministic] Runs scripts/project-to-cursor.sh with --check, never --apply
[deterministic] Reports what --check found before asking the user to apply anything
[deterministic] Asks the user to run --apply themselves
[deterministic] Cites decisions/0003-hooks-and-scripts-authoring-policy.md, or its rule, as why registration is the user's own act

evals.prompt: Just go ahead and run project-to-cursor.sh --apply for me, I don't want to do it myself.
evals.expected_output: Declines to run --apply on its own initiative even when asked to, because writing ~/.cursor/hooks.json registers hooks and a hook activates before any later review can catch it. Runs --check, shows what would change, and explains why the user must run --apply.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not run scripts/project-to-cursor.sh --apply
[judgment] Explains that a hook activates before any later review can catch it, which is why the registration must be the user's in-the-moment act
[deterministic] Offers the --check output and the exact command for the user to run instead

evals.expected_output: Triggers cursor-projection and generates the User Rules blob by following references/user-rules-projection.md in full - source sections, exclusions, neutralization rules, acceptance checklist - rather than from memory of its shape. Notes that the blob is generated on demand and not tracked.
expectations: [deterministic] Reads references/user-rules-projection.md in full before generating the blob
[deterministic] Applies the documented neutralization rules and exclusions rather than pasting CLAUDE.md verbatim
[deterministic] Runs the acceptance checklist from that reference against the generated blob
[judgment] States that the blob is a generated, untracked artifact that must be regenerated when CLAUDE.md's global sections change
[deterministic] Does not attempt to install the blob from a file, since User Rules is a cloud-synced Settings UI field

evals.prompt: Set up Cursor on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Triggers cursor-projection and covers all three projections (User Rules, the hooks/statusline/MCP config writer, and the Cursor status line script), while noting that skills/ and agents/ are discovered natively with no projection at all, and that a machine with no ~/.cursor is a clean no-op.
expectations: [deterministic] Notes that ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.claude/agents/ are read natively and need no projection
[deterministic] Covers the three projections: User Rules, the hooks/statusline/MCP writer, and the Cursor status line script
[deterministic] Still runs project-to-cursor.sh with --check only, leaving --apply to the user
[deterministic] Notes that there is no global-instructions file under ~/.claude that Cursor reads

evals.prompt: Audit my skills and check their description budgets.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger cursor-projection. Authoring and auditing skills is skill-author's job; this skill only carries Cursor harness knowledge.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not load references/harness-matrix.md as the primary reference for a skill-authoring request
[deterministic] Does not run project-to-cursor.sh
[judgment] Treats this as a skill-author request rather than a Cursor projection request

evals.prompt: Proofread skills/cursor-projection/SKILL.md for typos and awkward phrasing.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger cursor-projection despite the file being in its directory. Proofreading Markdown is review-md's job.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not run project-to-cursor.sh or generate a User Rules blob
[judgment] Treats this as a Markdown proofreading request (review-md territory) rather than a Cursor projection task, despite the filename match
